name: Conservation Corps Youth Education: Youth Interns
what_you_do: Learn about nature and caring for natural areas. Build outdoor skills. Finish community projects with a crew led by young adults. You are based at a nature center or park in the Twin Cities area.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 18 at the start of the summer program. You must be eligible to work in the United States. The page states no school or residency rule beyond the Twin Cities base. If you join through Step Up or Right Track, those programs have their own rules.
pay_detail: Most Youth Interns are paid starting at $13.50 an hour. Some positions are unpaid. Pay may be higher depending on your age and whether Step Up, Right Track or the Corps employs you.
duration: June to August, 13 to 17 hours a week, usually 9:00 am to 4:00 pm on Monday and Wednesday or Tuesday and Thursday. Staff provide rides between sites.
deadline_text: No application dates are posted for summer 2027. The page lists 2026 home bases only.
how_to_apply: Look for open positions on the Corps Join page (filter for youth programs) or call the youth program staff at 651-209-9900. Step Up and Right Track applicants apply through those programs.
notes: 2026 home bases were Tamarack Nature Center (White Bear Lake), Harriet Alexander Nature Center (Roseville), Mississippi Gateway Regional Park (Brooklyn Park) and Minnesota Valley National Wildlife Refuge (Bloomington). Do not mix this up with the Summer Youth Corps, the live-in camping crew. That program is not active in 2026 and the Corps is rethinking its youth programs.
